title: Fix: gcrypt linker-signed binary causes dyld crash on macOS 26
description: After 'make fuse', gcrypt.framework binary has flags=0x20002(adhoc,linker-signed) but Fuse.app binary has flags=0x10002(adhoc,runtime). macOS 26 dyld refuses to map the library with 'different Team IDs' error. Fix: change CODE_SIGN_IDENTITY from empty string (don't sign) to '-' (ad-hoc sign) and add ENABLE_HARDENED_RUNTIME=YES and CODE_SIGN_STYLE=Manual in libgcrypt.xcodeproj and audiofile.xcodeproj for all build configurations, so Xcode re-signs the binary with runtime flag during its own build phase.
close_reason: Moved framework re-signing (--identifier + -o runtime) from 'make adhoc' into 'make fuse' target in Makefile. Xcode CodeSignOnCopy produced a broken LC_CODE_SIGNATURE (stale datasize from DER entitlement blob) causing codesign --verify --strict and macOS 26 dyld to reject the bundle. make fuse now passes codesign --verify --deep --strict without needing make adhoc.

title: Fix: Add pre-enumeration HID usage filter to SDL joystick init
description: SDL_SYS_JoystickInit() in fuse/ui/cocoa/SDL_joystick/SDL_sysjoystick.c calls IOServiceMatching(kIOHIDDeviceKey) with no usage-page filter, causing macOS 10.15+ to trigger the Input Monitoring privacy permission. Fix by adding kHIDUsage_GD_Joystick/GamePad/MultiAxisController constraints to the hidMatchDictionary before calling IOServiceGetMatchingServices, so keyboards and other non-joystick HID devices are never enumerated. Also add NSInputMonitoringUsageDescription to Info-Fuse.plist as a fallback.

2. Migrate panes individually behind that shell, starting with the lowest-risk pane and proving the SwiftUI/AppKit bridge pattern.
3. Validate each migrated pane for settings binding parity, layout/resize behavior, and runtime behavior before moving to the next pane.
4. Continue replacing remaining pane content incrementally until all panes are hosted by SwiftUI, then reassess whether the outer shell should also be modernized.

title: Implement Makefile notarize and dist targets (Phase 2)
description:
Once the Apple Developer Program enrollment is confirmed (task fuse-for-macos-arm64-41j) and the Xcode project is updated to Developer ID signing (task fuse-for-macos-arm64-3iu), make two changes:

1. ADD --timestamp TO THE 'fuse' TARGET in the top-level Makefile
Apple's notarization service requires a secure timestamp on all signatures. Ad-hoc signing does not use timestamps, but Developer ID signing does. Add --timestamp to every codesign invocation in the 'fuse' target:

  codesign --sign "$(CODE_SIGN_IDENTITY)" --force --options runtime --timestamp \
      --identifier "net.sourceforge.fuse-for-macosx.gcrypt" ...
  (and similarly for audiofile, gcrypt.framework, audiofile.framework, plugins, and the app itself)

notarytool will reject binaries signed without a secure timestamp even if the signature is otherwise valid.

2. IMPLEMENT THE notarize AND dist TARGETS:

notarize target — full notarization workflow:
1. Create a temporary Fuse-notarize.zip from the built Fuse.app (transport container for notarytool)
2. Submit via 'xcrun notarytool submit --wait --keychain-profile $(NOTARYTOOL_PROFILE)', which blocks until Apple returns a result
3. Delete Fuse-notarize.zip (it is not the distribution artifact)
4. Staple the notarization ticket to Fuse.app via 'xcrun stapler staple'

dist target — create the final distribution zip:
- Depends on notarize
- Zip the stapled Fuse.app into Fuse.zip

NOTE on ordering: notarize must run before dist. The zip submitted to Apple is a temporary transport artifact. The distribution zip is created after stapling so the ticket is embedded in the app inside the zip. Gatekeeper verifies the staple on the .app itself, not the outer archive.

3. CONSIDER REMOVING com.apple.security.cs.disable-library-validation FROM Fuse.entitlements
This entitlement was added because macOS 26 enforces Library Validation (CS_FORCED_LV) on hardened-runtime processes without a Team ID, causing dyld to reject the ad-hoc-signed frameworks. With a real Developer ID and Team ID, all embedded binaries will share the same Team ID so Library Validation will pass without the exemption. Leaving the entitlement in weakens security unnecessarily. Remove it and verify the notarized build passes Gatekeeper before shipping.
notes: Implemented Makefile notarize and dist targets, added conditional codesign timestamps for Developer ID builds, and documented the release flow in README. Left Fuse.entitlements unchanged for now because removing disable-library-validation needs verification against a real notarized build; follow-up issue fuse-for-macos-arm64-qme tracks that work.

title: Set up Apple Developer account for notarization
description:
One-time setup steps required before notarization can work.

IMPORTANT: Use a dedicated Apple ID separate from your personal Apple ID. This prevents issues with one account (security lockout, billing problem, 2FA issue) from impacting the other. It also keeps the Developer ID certificate identity and the $99/year billing clearly separate from personal iCloud/App Store activity. You will need a dedicated email address for this Apple ID.

ENROLLMENT TIMELINE: Individual enrollment is typically confirmed within a few minutes to a few hours; Apple's official SLA is 24 hours. There is no manual identity verification step for individuals (unlike organisations). The main causes of delay are: (a) using an alias or nickname instead of your exact legal name in the Apple ID, or (b) paying with someone else's credit card, which triggers a request for government-issued photo ID. Use your legal name and your own credit card to avoid delays.

Steps:
1. Create a dedicated Apple ID for development at https://appleid.apple.com using a separate email address (e.g. fuse-dev@yourdomain.com). Use your exact legal first and last name — Apple uses this for identity verification and it will appear in Gatekeeper prompts shown to users. Enable two-factor authentication on the account.
2. Enroll the new Apple ID in the paid Apple Developer Program ($99/year) at https://developer.apple.com/enroll. Developer ID Application certificates — required for notarization — are only available with the paid tier. Pay with your own credit card to avoid triggering additional ID verification.
3. Wait for the confirmation email (typically minutes; up to 24 hours per Apple's SLA).
4. Sign in to Xcode with the new Apple ID: Xcode → Settings → Accounts → + → Apple ID.
5. In Xcode Accounts, select the new Apple ID and click 'Manage Certificates' → + → 'Developer ID Application' to create the signing certificate.
6. Note your Team ID: visible in Xcode Accounts, or at https://developer.apple.com/account under Membership Details. It is a 10-character uppercase alphanumeric string (e.g. XXXXXXXXXX). This is the value for DEVELOPMENT_TEAM in the Makefile.
7. Run 'make list-teams' (once the Makefile exists) to confirm the Developer ID Application certificate is visible to the keychain.
8. Create an app-specific password for the developer Apple ID at https://appleid.apple.com → Sign-In and Security → App-Specific Passwords. (Do not use your Apple ID password directly.)
9. Store notarytool credentials (one-time): xcrun notarytool store-credentials fuse-notarize --apple-id YOUR_DEV_APPLE_ID --team-id YOUR_TEAM_ID --password YOUR_APP_SPECIFIC_PASSWORD
close_reason: Completed Apple Developer account setup for notarization

title: Refactor: Replace SDL 1.x IOKit HID joystick driver with IOHIDManager API
description: The SDL 1.x joystick driver in fuse/ui/cocoa/SDL_joystick/SDL_sysjoystick.c uses the legacy IOMasterPort/IOServiceGetMatchingServices pattern. Replace with the modern IOHIDManager API (IOHIDManagerCreate, IOHIDManagerSetDeviceMatchingMultiple) with proper usage-page dictionaries for joystick/gamepad/multi-axis devices only. This is the SDL 2.x approach and fully avoids the TCC/Input Monitoring trigger without relying on pre-filtering heuristics. Resolves the underlying architectural cause of the privacy warning.
